# Await committed projection in Workstation grid witnesses

## Context

Three direct failures in the dock NL census require a Workspace-root motion pulse before checking post-splitter grid behavior: both `WorkstationGridRepaintNL` cases and the repeated-drag case in `WorkstationSplitterGridGeometryNL`.

The [worker/DOM trace](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17844#issuecomment-5594204500) at `335b2ca43a` records a root class interval of about 1 ms, no root DOM transition, and refresh settlement hundreds of milliseconds later. The [ten-cycle discriminator](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17844#issuecomment-5594404970) awaits the existing projection promise: all ten feed repaint checks pass, while all ten retained soft root-pulse assertions still fail.

## The Problem

A transient presentation class is being used as a mandatory completion witness. Worker class updates can coalesce before DOM application. A descendant overflow pulse is not a substitute: observed pulses began before the relevant refresh and cleared before it settled. The existing >20 px geometry check may also be satisfied by live resize preview.

These witnesses should reach their actual grid repaint/geometry assertions after the committed projection settles, including legitimate instant presentation.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Workspace.onDockZoneDocumentChange` schedules each committed projection on `refreshPromise`. Its completion hook includes the Workstation overflow, FLIP, host-update and participation waits.
- `InstanceService.callMethod` already resolves dotted paths and awaits the returned value. The fixture can call `app.callMethod(wsId, 'refreshPromise.then')`; no new engine or MCP API is needed.
- Typed projection failures can resolve an attempt while scheduling a replacement retry. The existing warning is retained by ConnectionService and readable through `app.getConsoleLogs`; assert its absence so a handled failure cannot count as clean settlement. A runtime negative control invokes the actual failure handler and must red this guard.
- The tested wait follows observation of the new committed split sizes. In the controlled ten-cycle run, a fresh traced refresh settled for each gesture, with waits of 244–441 ms.
- `DockFlip.play` returns false for instant presentation. `WorkstationDockFlipResizeNL` explicitly accepts a no-FLIP live-parity path and retains its own visual-discontinuity oracle. Those animation-specific assertions remain separate.
- The Main trace observed visible documents, valid 280 ms tokens, six markers, and false play results in every cycle. It does not establish which instant exit was taken.

## The Fix

Replace the three positive root-motion barriers with the existing committed-projection wait after the semantic change has been observed. Remove their unused observer helpers/state. Preserve each witness's existing input mechanism and every actual repaint, geometry, identity, error and residue assertion.

Update settlement comments to describe the owner being awaited. Do not equate a source-class interval, a descendant pulse, a changed live-preview width or a generic VDOM cycle with committed projection completion.

| Grid proof | Existing visible-record repaint and keyed worker/header/cell comparisons | Same workload, repeated directions, identities, tolerances and residue checks | Real drift remains a failure | Existing oracle documentation | Current-head headed E2E receipts |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three root-pulse barriers in the two named files use the existing projection settlement after the new semantic split is observed; unused observer scaffolding is removed.
- [ ] Preserve the ten feed cycles, scale-record mutation, both-direction geometry sequence, identity/tolerance checks, transform/fixed-stage cleanup and error assertions. Preserve the separate deterministic transformed-geometry control.
- [ ] Prove the wait belongs to a fresh post-gesture projection rather than a previous resolved promise; retain the controlled receipt and a failure-capable settlement check.
- [ ] Run both complete E2E files with the explicit Brain runtime and custom config at the candidate head. Preserve baseline failures and report any newly exposed later defect separately. No whole-film or native matrix claim follows.

## Out of Scope

Production motion changes, forcing a visible frame, new engine/NL APIs, changing input provenance, broad five-spec rewrites, the adjacent EdgeSplitter/NestedColumn failures, and closing any actual repaint or film defect by association.

## Avoided Traps

Do not broaden the observer to any descendant, remove the positive barrier entirely, add sleeps, weaken the grid assertions, or treat false FLIP as a broken animation contract without its own evidence. A plain promiseUpdate does not await a deferred projection.

## Decision Record impact

No ADR or production contract change; this consumes existing projection ownership.
